transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support. My name is Simon. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Simon. I am experiencing a persistent, infuriating technical problem with our broadband. Every single time our landline telephone rings with an incoming phone call, our broadband Hub instantly drops its DSL sync and the internet disconnects completely! It happens every time someone rings us!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you troubleshoot that line interference drop issue, Leanne. Can you please confirm the landline telephone number associated with your broadband service?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Leanne. And what is the equipment serial number printed on the rear barcode label of your Hub?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The serial number is HUB-552-1980. Simon, I work from home as an accredited crisis counsellor for a national suicide prevention helpline! Vulnerable, desperate callers in acute distress telephone me for emergency emotional de-escalation, while I simultaneously need stable internet to coordinate emergency welfare dispatches with local police and ambulance services! When our phone rings and the internet drops, I lose connection to the dispatch system and vulnerable people's lives are literally hanging in the balance! I am terrified that someone will die because of this connection dropping!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: VDSL high-frequency carrier modulation is sensitive to ringer AC voltage induced across unbalanced copper telephone pairs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please Simon, I need this interference stopped immediately so I can take crisis shifts safely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, your VDSL broadband connection suffers an immediate DSL sync dropout every time an incoming telephone call rings your landline handset, disrupting your emergency suicide crisis counselling service, and you need the line interference resolved. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happens and why it is so critical to fix.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is your S-Net Hub and telephone handset currently connected to the wall socket? Are you using a microfilter dongle or a filtered faceplate?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both the Hub and the telephone base station are plugged into a little white plastic plug-in microfilter adapter that plugs into the wall socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How many years has that plug-in microfilter been in continuous service?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It was installed when we moved into this house about seven years ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Passive surface-mount capacitors inside microfilters degrade over time; when seventy-five volts AC ringing current hits the line, high-frequency VDSL signals leak across the voice coil.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the seventy-five volt telephone ring voltage is blowing the internet off the copper line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ring generator AC voltage spikes into the high-frequency band above twenty-five kilohertz, overwhelming the modem's trellis decoder.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that mean the microfilter has completely failed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The internal low-pass passive LC filter circuit has suffered dielectric breakdown on the capacitor bank.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we test without that old microfilter right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you have a spare microfilter from an old router package in your home?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look in the hallway drawer... yes! I found a brand-new sealed S-Net microfilter in plastic wrapping!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unwrap the new microfilter, unplug the old one from the master socket, and plug the new microfilter directly into the wall.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Swapping the filter now... plugged the new microfilter into the socket, grey DSL lead into the Hub port, and telephone lead into the phone port.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub power and broadband indicators will re-initialize VDSL handshake.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Broadband light is flashing amber... now solid blue! The internet is back online!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us perform a live ringer stress test by ringing your landline from our exchange diagnostic test console.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Go ahead, ring the telephone and let us see if the Hub stays blue.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Triggering test call to 01603 892104 now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The phone in the hallway is ringing loudly! Ring, ring... looking at the Hub... the light stayed completely solid blue! It didn't drop out at all!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms the dielectric capacitor breakdown in the legacy microfilter was the sole point of failure, Leanne.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What an enormous weight off my shoulders! I can take my crisis counselling shift tonight without fearing dropped lines!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the broadband drop when you dial out on the telephone, or only when an incoming call rings?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Simon, as I told you in my very first sentence, it only dropped when someone rang us! And we just proved that replacing the filter fixed it completely!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize Leanne, that was a standard procedural verification prompt on my fault flow chart.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please pay attention to what we have already discussed and tested.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. To ensure permanent protection against ringer leakage, S-Net can dispatch an interstitial filtered master faceplate.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How does a filtered faceplate differ from the plug-in microfilter?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An NTE5c filtered faceplate clips directly onto your master wall socket, isolating all internal extension copper wiring permanently from VDSL frequencies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does it require an engineer to fit or can I clip it on myself?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It is a tool-less push-fit faceplate designed for customer self-installation in thirty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please dispatch one of those filtered faceplates so we have the best permanent protection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Internal telephone extension wiring beyond the master test socket is strictly your own domestic property responsibility; S-Net holds zero liability for home wiring defects.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand that, Simon. I am just asking for the faceplate hardware that S-Net provides to customers.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have ordered an Openreach NTE5c MK4 filtered faceplate under order REF-881920 on Royal Mail tracked forty-eight delivery.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When will the faceplate arrive in the post?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Delivery will occur by Wednesday afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let us check the line speed now with the new microfilter in place.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The line is currently synced at seventy-one megabits per second downstream with an SNR noise margin of six point eight decibels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Seventy-one megabits is faster than it has been in months.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check the downstream interleaving depth on your line profile to ensure impulsive noise from domestic appliances does not cause CRC errors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking our line profile... what is the current interleaving delay on the line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The line profile is set to dynamic fast-path interleaving with a four-millisecond delay, which balances low latency with noise immunity.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Four milliseconds is wonderfully fast for our emergency dispatch coordination tools.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Eliminating the leaky capacitor restored three megabits of high-frequency attenuation loss across the DMT sub-channels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the ringer circuit produce any interference on telephone audio quality?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: With the new low-pass filter operating at full attenuation, voice frequencies below four kilohertz remain completely isolated from high-speed data.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Listening to the telephone dial tone right now... it is completely silent with zero background buzz or hiss.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the common-mode copper rejection ratio is operating above sixty decibels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test opening my suicide crisis helpline dispatch software on my work laptop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead, verify secure socket gateway connectivity.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Logging into the NHS crisis dispatch portal... connection established in three seconds! All patient queue telemetry is live!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The encrypted VPN tunnel is maintaining steady thirty-millisecond latency.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me total reassurance that tonight's counselling shift will run without interruption.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to reconfirm, the landline telephone number receiving the faceplate pack is 01603 892104.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 01603 892104. That is completely correct.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you experience any further drops on extension phones, do not contact S-Net as domestic bell wire maintenance is strictly your private problem.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There are no extension sockets in this house, so that won't be an issue. But you really could be more polite, Simon.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Simon, what should I do with the old microfilter? Does S-Net want it posted back or...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bin it. Your broadband is working. Thank you for choosing S-Net. Have a good day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Simon, don't hang up... hello? He hung up on me!
